$comment: GENERATED by scripts/generate-coverage-matrix.ts — do not edit; run npm run gen:coverage-matrix. A status says a registered test EXISTS for the cell and what kind of expected value it checks; it is not a pass. See rules.

rules.cell: A capability cell is one (mechanism, operation, parameter set, sign variant). Mechanism, operation (from CKF_ flags) and key-size range are DISCOVERED from the running engine (C_GetMechanismList + C_GetMechanismInfo); parameter sets, sign variants and boundaries are DECLARED in capability-map.json and kept only when the parameter set falls inside the engine-reported key-size range.
rules.denominator: Denominator (per engine) = advertised capability cells: the engine lists the mechanism, sets the CKF_ flag for the operation, and the declared parameter set falls inside its reported key-size range. Cells the engine does not advertise, and declared capabilities no PKCS #11 mechanism can express, are counted separately as unsupported and shown — never dropped.
rules.status: Cell status = the strongest evidence class among registered test cases that exercise the cell on that engine (order: acvts-issued > nist-reference > standard-kat > oracle > differential > round-trip > behavior-only). No registered case = untested. Not advertised = unsupported. A status says a test EXISTS; it is not a pass.
rules.covered: Covered (per polarity) = at least 2 distinct registered cases of that polarity exercise the cell AND, for positive, at least one of them checks an externally expected value (acvts-issued, nist-reference, standard-kat or oracle). A cell is covered overall only when positive, negative, boundary and state-error are all covered.
rules.sampled: Sampled = at least one registered case, but the covered rule is not met. One happy-path case is always "sampled", never "covered" (plan Q5).
rules.polarity: Polarities are counted separately: a positive case never counts toward negative, boundary or state-error. Boundary = a registered case whose recorded parameters hit a declared boundary of the cell (e.g. context length 0 or 255, empty message); it may also be a positive or negative case. State-error = a case asserting a PKCS #11 state or argument error.
rules.parity: Parity = both engines have a RECORDED PASS of the same registered case on the same artifact kind. Skipped, unsupported and not-run never count as a pass, and a recorded result counts only for the exact artifact (sha256) the mechanism inventory records. Rows with no such pair are "not established".
rules.artifacts: Artifact kinds are reported separately: wasm (the two shipped WebAssembly engines — registered tests run in the browser), native, hardware. Native and hardware targets have not been run: they are "not run" and never counted as pass.
rules.dimensions: Plan G-3 — two further columns per cell, from the same registered cases. Algorithm correctness = cases whose expected value is checked (acvts-issued, nist-reference, standard-kat, oracle, differential, round-trip; state-error cases excluded); covered when at least 2 distinct cases exist and one has an externally expected value. PKCS #11 API behaviour = cases that assert only PKCS #11 behaviour (behavior-only evidence: return codes, operation state, buffers, attributes) plus every state-error case; covered when at least 2 distinct cases exist and one is a state-error case. Neither column says a test passed.
rules.inventory: Per engine and artifact kind the matrix counts, separately: advertised cells (the denominator — C_GetMechanismList × operation × parameter set × variant), registered cells (≥ 1 registered case, by evidence status), cells with a recorded pass, with a recorded fail, and with a recorded skip (the engine did not advertise a mechanism the case needs, so it was not run), unsupported cells (not advertised) and untested cells (advertised, no registered case). A skip is never a pass and is never folded into untested.

definitions.numerator: Numerators (per engine, per polarity) = advertised cells whose level is covered, sampled or untested under the rules below; covered + sampled + untested = the denominator. Per-status numerators count advertised cells by their strongest registered evidence class.
definitions.denominator: Denominator (per engine) = advertised capability cells: the engine lists the mechanism, sets the CKF_ flag for the operation, and the declared parameter set falls inside its reported key-size range. Cells the engine does not advertise, and declared capabilities no PKCS #11 mechanism can express, are counted separately as unsupported and shown — never dropped.

openGaps.title: ML-DSA hedged signing with a caller-supplied rnd is not reachable through PKCS #11
openGaps.detail: CK_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT carries hedgeVariant and context only; there is no parameter for an explicit rnd, so NIST hedged sigGen expected signatures cannot be reproduced on either engine. Shown in the workbench as an explicit skip (mldsa-skip-hedged-rnd-*) and here as unsupported rows.

openGaps.title: ECDSA P-521 NIST sample failed on C++ — hub CKA_EC_POINT encoding (fixed hub-side)
openGaps.detail: Root cause (triage 2026-09-24): hsm_importECPublicKey wrote the DER OCTET STRING length of the 133-byte P-521 point as the single byte 0x85, which DER reads as '5 length octets follow'; the C++ engine parsed a garbage CKA_EC_POINT and rejected the NIST ACVP-Server ECDSA-SigVer-FIPS186-5 sample (workbench §33), while Rust passed because it reads the raw CKA_VALUE copy. Hub adapter bug, not an engine defect. Fixed by the X.690 long-form length (softhsm/helpers derOctetString); the re-recorded run shows the case passing on both engines. Kept on record until the release freeze re-captures evidence on the browser host.

openGaps.title: SUCI key-injection helper is rejected by the C++ engine
openGaps.detail: hsm_injectTestKey unwraps the raw EC scalar with C_UnwrapKeyAuthenticated using a template that carries CKA_EC_PARAMS; the C++ engine rejects it with CKR_ATTRIBUTE_READ_ONLY (the same unwrap without CKA_EC_PARAMS succeeds). katRunner suci-profile-b steps 1-2 (import only, not registered) therefore error on C++; steps 3-7 import with C_CreateObject and pass on both engines. The KAT surfaces run the Rust engine. Hub helper limitation.

openGaps.title: PKCS #11 v3.2 gives no single key-handle / key-type code for C_DecapsulateKey — not probed
openGaps.detail: §5.18.9 lists CKR_UNWRAPPING_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID and CKR_UNWRAPPING_KEY_TYPE_INCONSISTENT (not CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID / CKR_KEY_TYPE_INCONSISTENT), while §5.1.6 says the UNWRAPPING_* codes "can only be returned by C_UnwrapKey". With no single specified value there is no key-handle or key-type probe for C_DecapsulateKey (the engines differ: C++ returns CKR_UNWRAPPING_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID for handle 0, Rust CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID). Likewise C_WrapKey, C_UnwrapKey, C_DeriveKey and C_EncapsulateKey require the usage attribute but do not list CKR_KEY_FUNCTION_NOT_PERMITTED, so no key-usage probe exists for them. Specification ambiguity, not an engine defect. Recorded by the G-8 error-path probes (errorPathCatalog.ts / errorPathProbes.ts) in run-results/wasm-node-errorPathProbes.json; the rows stay failing — the assertion is the PKCS #11 v3.2 value and is not loosened.

openGaps.title: Classical NIST reference samples cover only what the pinned upstream samples register
openGaps.detail: The pinned ACVP-Server@975de31e samples bound what WS-E can claim: ACVP-AES-GCM-1.0 registers AES-128 only (IV 96/120, tag 128/32, payload/AAD 0/120 bits) — AES-192/256-GCM, 64-bit tags and other lengths have no NIST case; HMAC 2.0 registers macLen 80..160 bits — no full-length (untruncated) tag, so CKM_<hash>_HMAC (non-general) has no NIST case; EDDSA-SigVer-1.0 carries no context string (contexts are exercised only through the EDDSA-SigGen-1.0 byte-match cases of eddsa_siggen_acvp_test); ECDSA SHA2-512/256 and SHAKE groups have no PKCS#11 v3.2 CKM_ECDSA_<hash> mechanism (skip rows). Checked again 2026-09-25 (GitHub API, gap-closure P5): 975de31e (2026-08-12, "RELEASE/v1.1.0.43 including hotfix patches") is still the head of usnistgov/ACVP-Server master and the only other branch (jbrock24-patch-1, 2024) changes the README only, so no newer upstream commit carries AES-192/256-GCM or full-length HMAC tag samples; the scope gap stays.

openGaps.title: Classical families still without NIST ACVP-Server cases after WS-E and gap-closure P5
openGaps.detail: Closed by gap-closure P5 (2026-09-25): HKDF (hkdf_acvp_test, KDA-HKDF-Sp800-56Cr2), SP 800-108 KBKDF (kbkdf_acvp_test, KDF 1.0 counter / feedback / double pipeline), ECDSA/EdDSA KeyVer (ecdsa_/eddsa_keyver_acvp_test, the key is used: sign with d, verify with the point), ECDSA SigGen verify-back (functional round-trip + independent oracle; NIST r, s are not reproducible because C_Sign draws its own nonce), EdDSA SigGen byte-match, the alternate-version SHA-2 MCT and full 100-iteration MCTs for SHA-2/SHA-3 and AES-CBC (sha_mct_full_test, aescbc_mct_full_test). Still open: ANSI X9.63 KDF on a caller-supplied Z — not expressible through PKCS #11 (declaredUnreachable x963-kdf-caller-z, gap x963-kdf-caller-z-no-mechanism); SHA LDT (1 GiB expanded message); HKDF multi-expansion groups; KBKDF with CMAC-TDES, HMAC-SHA2-512/224, /256 or bit-oriented output lengths; ECDSA/EdDSA KeyGen and deterministic ECDSA SigGen (no PKCS #11 input for the random / RFC 6979 nonce). The older HKDF/PBKDF2/X9.63/KBKDF workbench rows keep their published-standard / oracle / round-trip labels.

openGaps.title: ANSI X9.63 KDF on a caller-supplied shared secret has no PKCS #11 mechanism
openGaps.detail: PKCS #11 v3.2 defines the X9.63 KDF only as the CK_EC_KDF_TYPE of CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE and related ECDH mechanisms (§6.3.16), applied to the shared secret the token derives from its own key pair; no mechanism accepts a caller-supplied Z, so the NIST kdf-components-ansix9.63-1.0 cases (Z, sharedInfo -> keyData) cannot be executed. Shown as the workbench skip row x963-kdf-unsupported and the capability-map declaredUnreachable row x963-kdf-caller-z. The KDF itself is exercised inside ECDH derivation (section 25, round-trip only).

openGaps.title: C++: SP 800-108 KDFs ignore where the caller places the counter in the PRF input
openGaps.detail: With the PKCS #11 v3.2 §6.42 data-parameter layout the NIST KDF 1.0 cases require, the C++ engine derives the wrong key whenever the counter is not in its fixed position: counter mode with the ITERATION_VARIABLE after or in the middle of the fixed data, and feedback / double-pipeline with a COUNTER before the chaining value or after the fixed data (kbkdf_acvp_test, 12 rows per run: HMAC-SHA2-256 and CMAC-AES128). 'Before fixed data' (and no counter) layouts byte-match NIST for every PRF. The engine appears to place the counter first (counter mode) or right after K(i-1)/A(i) (feedback / double pipeline) regardless of the CK_PRF_DATA_PARAM order. Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

openGaps.title: Rust: feedback and double-pipeline KBKDF reject the mandatory ITERATION_VARIABLE data parameter
openGaps.detail: PKCS #11 v3.2 §6.42.4/§6.42.5 make CK_SP800_108_ITERATION_VARIABLE mandatory in feedback and double-pipeline mode (pValue NULL, ulValueLen 0; §6.42.2). The Rust engine returns CKR_MECHANISM_PARAM_INVALID for every such layout, so all 38 feedback / double-pipeline NIST KDF 1.0 rows fail. Probed 2026-09-25: without the ITERATION_VARIABLE entry the engine accepts the parameters and reproduces NIST except where the counter precedes the chaining value. Counter mode (ITERATION_VARIABLE with a counter format) is correct in every location. The hub keeps the specification layout; the existing sections 27/29 call the feedback mechanism without the ITERATION_VARIABLE. Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

openGaps.title: C++: invalid ECDSA / EdDSA public points are imported and used without validation
openGaps.detail: The NIST keyVer cases with a point not on the curve or a coordinate out of range (ecdsa_keyver_acvp_test P-256/384/521, eddsa_keyver_acvp_test Ed25519/Ed448: 10 points) are accepted by C_CreateObject and C_VerifyInit, and C_Verify then returns CKR_SIGNATURE_INVALID as for any wrong signature — no FIPS 186-5 / SP 800-56A public-key validation happens on import or use (PKCS #11 v3.2 §4.1.1 would return CKR_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID at creation). Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

openGaps.title: Rust: invalid public points are refused only at C_Verify, with a code C_Verify does not list
openGaps.detail: The Rust engine imports the 10 invalid NIST keyVer points (C_CreateObject CKR_OK) and accepts C_VerifyInit, then C_Verify returns CKR_KEY_TYPE_INCONSISTENT — not among the §5.15.2 C_Verify return values. The keyVer rows pass (the point is refused with a key error), but validation belongs at C_CreateObject (§4.1.1 CKR_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID) or C_VerifyInit.

openGaps.title: Rust: Ed25519ph / Ed448ph signing ignores the CK_EDDSA_PARAMS context
openGaps.detail: C_Sign(CKM_EDDSA, phFlag = true, non-empty context) on the Rust engine produces the Ed25519ph / Ed448ph signature for an EMPTY context: all 8 preHash NIST EDDSA-SigGen-1.0 cases (contexts 96–248 bytes) differ from NIST, and @noble/curves ed25519ph verifies the Rust output without the context and rejects it with it. Pure Ed25519 / Ed448 with contexts byte-match. The C++ engine matches all 16 cases. Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

PKCS #11 v3.2 §6.67.7 defines no CKM_HASH_ML_DSA_<hash> mechanism for SHA2-512/224 or SHA2-512/256, so no engine can advertise one; the NIST ACVP sigVer groups for these hashes are listed in mldsa_sigver_test.json notExecuted.

CK_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT carries hedgeVariant and context only; PKCS #11 v3.2 has no parameter for an explicit rnd, so the NIST hedged sigGen expected signatures cannot be reproduced through either engine (plan D2-4).

No PKCS #11 v3.2 mechanism exposes the internal interface on a raw M′ (CKM_ML_DSA always applies the external domain-separation prefix); NIST groups with signatureInterface=internal and externalMu=false are listed in the vector files notExecuted.

PKCS #11 v3.2 applies the X9.63 KDF only as the CK_EC_KDF_TYPE of the ECDH derivations (§6.3.16, CKD_<hash>_KDF), to the Z the token computes from its own key pair and the peer point; no mechanism takes a caller-supplied Z, so the NIST (Z, sharedInfo) -> keyData cases cannot be driven (workbench skip row x963-kdf-unsupported).
